text:
Alex W: Heads-up — overnight SLO drift on embed-p99 in eu-west. I did a quick sweep at 03:30 UTC and rolled back the canary; latency looks back to normal. Sharing what I did / blockers / plan below.

Maya R: Thanks Alex. Do we have the raw numbers? p50/p95/p99? :eyes:

Samir G: p50 stayed ~20ms, p95 ticked to ~120ms, p99 jumped from ~190ms to ~620ms for ~6 minutes around 03:20 UTC. Alerts fired but debounce prevented repeat noise.

Alex W: Reverted canary at 03:28; metrics normalized by 03:34. Quick log check on the affected node showed repeated full-GC cycles and OOM-kernel messages. Example run I used:
```
kubectl -n inference logs pod/gpu-ded-07 --since=15m | grep -E "GC|OOM|evict"
```

Lee H: Can you paste the canary config? Wondering if batch size or token-window changed.

Alex W: Canary diff shows batch_size bumped from 32 -> 64 in the canary YAML (PR 4231). Also injector bump to max_seq=4096. Not ideal for this route.

Maya R: That PR was autoscaler + batching tweak. @Samir G — can you check autoscaler metrics? Could the scaling lag + larger batches cause the GC spike?

Samir G: On it. Quick note: autoscaler reported scale events + 2 failed pods due to GPU driver mismatch. Blocker: need to confirm driver version alignment across the pool. I'll tail the autoscaler-controller logs and the node events.

Nina P: I also saw KV-cache eviction pressure around 03:18 on eu-west-2. If prefix cache warmed out, more requests hit the model full compute path which amplifies GC pressure. Suggest adding a short warmup cache policy for the canary.

Oncall-Bot: Alert cleared for SLO-EMBED-P99 in eu-west. Incident ticket created: https://tracker.redwood/INC-2026-298 — assigned to eng-sre.

Alex W: Plan for today: 1) Pin canary batch_size back to 32 and roll a tuned canary with lower max_seq, 2) add driver ver check in deploy pipeline (Samir), 3) add warmup-cache TTL tweak for canary routes (Nina). I'll open three PRs and link here.

Maya R: Thanks. If you want I can help with the warmup tests in staging this afternoon. :thumbsup:

Samir G: Will look for driver mismatch notes and post a short summary. If I need hardware team, I'll ping infra-channel.

Lee H: Quick ask — please add a runbook note under "canary->latency" about checking batch_size and KV warmup steps. Saves time on next wakeup.

Alex W: Agreed — will add runbook entry and the rollback checklist. Putting the PR links in this thread once created.

Nina P: Access note: I granted Samir access to the private autoscaler dashboard. Samir, try again and ping if still blocked.

Samir G: Got it, I can access now. Starting deeper dig and will update by EOD.

Maya R: Sounds good. Thanks all — ping here for any quick follow-ups.

Alex W: Closing the async check-in. TL;DR: revert canary batch_size, add driver check, warmup-cache tweak, runbook update.
